mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This effect is consistent across historical data without requiring specific thresholds.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 7.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 7.5% in a 3-month window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of industrial production growth exceeding 0.5% quarter-over-quarter, supply chain constraints ease and corporate capacity utilization improves, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% QoQ, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer confidence and residential investment, which correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to immediate economic momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may prompt central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market with rising wage pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to inflation concerns and potential rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp MoM, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods when the federal funds rate is below 1.0%, a further decline in the rate signals aggressive monetary easing that boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
